grammar.title: Verb + -ing or To-Infinitive (want to, enjoy -ing)
grammar.explanation:
When one verb follows another, the second verb is either **to + verb** or **verb-ing**. It depends on the **first** verb: I **want to go**. I **enjoy going**.

Some verbs always take **to**: **want**, **decide**, **hope**, **plan**, **promise**. For example: I **plan to visit** my family in April.

Some verbs always take **-ing**: **enjoy**, **finish**, **mind**, **keep**. For example: She **enjoys reading** in the afternoon.

After **like**, **love**, **hate** and **start**, both forms are fine: I love **to swim**. I love **swimming**.

There is no simple rule. Learn the verbs in each group, and check the grammar quiz!

practice.q: Rewrite using 'enjoy': I like cooking in the afternoon.
practice.a: I enjoy cooking in the afternoon.

practice.q: Rewrite using 'want to': I would like to visit my grandparents in April.
practice.a: I want to visit my grandparents in April.

practice.q: Rewrite using 'decided to': We made the choice to stay home two days ago.
practice.a: We decided to stay home two days ago.

practice.q: Rewrite using 'finished': Did you complete reading the book?
practice.a: Have you finished reading the book?
